# lab-zone

The lab's DNS zone, offered downward so every cluster resolves against one.

<!-- Generated by nix build .#referencePages -->

## Inputs

| input | type | default | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| port | null or 16 bit unsigned integer; between 0 and 65535 (both inclusive) | `the lab's slot in `lib/allocation.nix`` | Port the zone's server answers on: what `lab-dns` publishes and what a pod forwards to.  Null takes the lab's allocated slot, which is every lab in this tree. Set it to move off one — the allocation spans 5300-5555, which contains 5353 (mDNS) and 5355 (LLMNR, held by systemd-resolved on most Linux hosts), so two names in 256 land on a port that looks free and is not.  One number in one place. `lab-dns` publishes on what this says rather than taking a port of its own; it was two options, `lab.dns.port` defaulting to `lab.dns.hostPort`, with the lab handing each to a different floe.  |
| zone | string | *(required)* | The lab's DNS zone, as `lab.test`. Required. |

## Requires

| hole | signature | what it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| network | [LAB_NETWORK](../signatures/LAB_NETWORK.md) | The docker network a lab's containers share, and the gateway address on it. |

## Provides

| provision | signature | what it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| zone | [DNS_ZONE](../signatures/DNS_ZONE.md) | The lab's DNS zone and the server authoritative for it. The only fully portable signature. |

## What it emits

Rendered by `every-floe` as the lab unit `zone`. A unit of the lab
installs nothing into a cluster, and its provisions are sealed inside the
lab's inclusion — so its declaration above is its interface.
